features.name: share_comments_open_with_op_quote
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments open with a blockquote (starting with >) that quotes the OP's own text?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). For each comment, decide whether its first content (after leading whitespace) is a blockquote line beginning with '>' AND the quoted text reproduces or closely paraphrases wording from the OP's title or argument. Comments opening with '>' that quote another commenter or an external source, or comments with a quote only later, do not count. Compare against title/argument only to identify the quoted speaker; ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports as evidence. Output = (count qualifying comments)/(total comments), in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; unparseable -> null.

features.name: any_comment_starts_with_gt
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment begin with the '>' blockquote character?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; return 1 if any comment string, after lstrip(), startswith('>'), else 0. Empty list -> 0; missing/malformed -> null. Raw text match; does not check whom is quoted.

h0: share_comments_open_with_op_quote has no association with delta.
h1: Higher share_comments_open_with_op_quote is associated with lower probability of delta (OP view change).
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the row-level delta outcome; no per-comment outcomes exist, so this is a row-level association, not a comment-level comparison of quote-opening vs other comments. 'Strongly' is not tested beyond sign. Row share is confounded by number of comments. Unordered comments; OC_comments may include text with outcome announcements. Whether '>' text quotes OP requires semantic judgment; any_comment_starts_with_gt is a mechanical looser companion measure not used in the test (can be swapped into the rhs).
